subject: Seraph Systems inference discovery — action grid and topology follow-up
messages:
From: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@seraphsys.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@seraphsys.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Discovery follow-up — Seraph inference needs

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can plan internally:

- Primary pain: production latency spikes during end-of-day processing and unpredictable token costs when throughput increases.
- Secondary: KV cache invalidation and session stickiness are causing token duplication and higher compute.
- Goal: Reduce p95 generation latency to under 200ms for our medium-length prompts (avg 256 tokens) and get a predictable per-token cost model for budgeting.

Can you send a concise post-call summary that includes: the options you see for meeting the p95 target, what model variants work best given our 70B instruction-tuned family, and a proposed mutual action plan for the next 3 sprints? Also, Elena wanted a rough topology sketch (hosted vs VPC) for security review.

Thanks —
Tom
CTO, Seraph Systems

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@seraphsys.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@seraphsys.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — Seraph inference needs

Tom — appreciate the clear summary. Putting answers below and attaching an "action grid" (seraph_action_grid_v1.xlsx) that maps pains to short/medium/long solutions and owners. High level: feel like we can hit your goals with a combination of model-variant routing, KV prefix caching, and a dedicated GPU pool for peak windows.

Observed pain points (from call):
- Latency spikes during batch processing windows (end-of-day peaks).
- Token duplication from incomplete session cache eviction logic.
- Cost unpredictability when tail traffic scales.

Proposed short-term SLO targets (option A/B):
- Option A (latency-first): p50 40-60ms, p95 <= 180-200ms for 256-token prompts (single-stream with continuous batching disabled for low-latency paths).
- Option B (cost-balanced): p50 60-90ms, p95 <= 250ms with batching and ~20% token-cost reduction via micro-batching + KV caching.

Model guidance:
- Primary: 70B instruction-tuned, compiled with 4-bit quantization (QLoRA-style) — best latency/cost tradeoff for your workload; expected inference memory per replica ~40-48GB depending on quantization.
- Fallback: 13B FP16 for sub-100ms p50-critical routes, used as autoscale fallback to preserve availability during load spikes.

Topology options (summary) — see topology_draft_v2.png:
1) Hosted Dedicated Pool (recommended initially): Redwood-managed GPU fleet dedicated to Seraph — predictable throughput, SLA-backed, fast onboarding.
2) Private VPC (recommended for long-term/compliance): control plane managed by Redwood, data plane in your VPC with HSM/KMS integration — slightly higher latency tail but stronger control.
3) Hybrid: Dedicated pool for day-to-day, spillover to Private VPC during scheduled bulk processing windows.

Immediate next steps (mutual action plan):
- Redwood: send action grid + topology sketch (attached) — owner: Rishi (done).
- Seraph: confirm peak window times and sample logs for a week — owner: Elena — target by Mon 11/29.
- Joint: 60-minute technical deep dive to lock SLOs and cost model — propose Mon 11/30 10:00am PT.

I've attached the initial action grid and a lightweight SLO matrix (slo_matrix.csv) that maps traffic buckets to recommended routing policies. Marissa from our infra team will follow with kernel/quantization notes in the deep-dive.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0199

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Tom Briggs <tom.briggs@seraphsys.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Elena Park <elena@seraphsys.com>
Date: 2026-11-25T11:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up — Seraph inference needs (technical deep-dive notes)

Tom / Rishi — following Rishi's notes, I pulled together an ops-focused readout for the Monday deep-dive. Key assumptions: avg prompt length 256 tokens, 30% of requests include context (session KV) that benefits from prefix caching, expected burst QPS 350 with sustained 80 QPS.

Technical summary / recommendations:
- Model: 70B instruction-tuned compiled to 4-bit int (we've seen ~2.5-3x token/sec improvement vs fp16 on A100-like hardware when kernels are optimized). Memory per replica: ~42GB.
- Latency targets: for your stated target (p95 <= 200ms): we recommend a 2-path routing policy:
  - Latency path (no batching): route to low-concurrency replicas pinned for <120ms p50, aim p95 <= 180ms; use KV prefix cache pinned to those replicas for session-affinity.
  - Cost path (batching enabled): route best-effort traffic into batched workers with dynamic batch sizing (goal p95 <= 250ms).
- Throughput capacity: estimate concurrent token throughput per GPU replica ~1.8k tokens/sec (70B 4-bit, optimized kernels). For 350 QPS with avg 256 tokens -> ~89,600 tokens/sec total -> ~50 replicas nominal with headroom for peaks. (We'll refine after you provide traffic histograms.)
- Autoscaling & fallbacks: use predictive autoscaling around known end-of-day windows; configure immediate fallback to 13B FP16 variants when queue depth exceeds threshold to preserve tail latency and reduce queuing.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache TTL policies should align with session lengths; recommend 6-12 hour eviction windows for high-stickiness flows, and a negative-cache for 404/no-context to avoid duplicate caching.

Security/ops notes for topology draft:
- Hosted Dedicated: we can preserve request metadata, encrypt at rest, and integrate with your SSO + audit logs.
- VPC: supports HSM-backed keys; we will provide config templates for subnet and NACLs. Expect a small network egress variability (~10-15ms tail).

Attachments included: topology_draft_v2.png (sketch), slo_matrix.csv (traffic buckets to routing policy).

Open questions for the Monday call:
1) Can you share a representative 24-hour traffic histogram and a list of scheduled batch windows?
2) Do you have hard compliance constraints that require on-prem data residency vs VPC?
3) Who will be the procurement contact for a Dedicated commitment?

I'll bring a sample capacity model and a back-of-envelope cost estimate once we have histograms.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Infra Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0177
